public_rationale: The post (28 April 2026) assumes 15.2GW under construction, a PUE of about 1.35 and $14 million per megawatt. From those inputs the arithmetic roughly works: 15.2GW divided by 1.35 is about 11.26GW, and 11.2GW times $14 million per MW is $156.8 billion. The core of the claim is that this revenue is 'required to actually make these data centers worth it.' The passage applies $14 million per MW as annual revenue but gives no basis for that figure. It does not define 'worth it' as payback, profit or covering cost. The packet did not find a source for the 15.2GW input. BloombergNEF (e1) counted about 23.1GW of IT capacity under construction worldwide at the end of September 2025, including 15.9GW in the US. Its scope and date differ from his figure, so it neither confirms nor refutes it. Without a defined standard for 'required,' only the arithmetic can be checked, and the claim cannot be graded.
limitations: The packet did not find the TD Cowen note behind the $14 million per MW figure or the tracker behind the 15.2GW figure.
The arithmetic check was done from his stated inputs, not from an outside source.
The BloombergNEF count has a different scope and date and cannot test his capacity input.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Assuming a PUE of about 1.35 (roughly 11.2GW of critical IT) and $14 million per megawatt, the 15.2GW of data centers under construction need around $156.8 billion in annual GPU rental revenue to be worth it.

statement.excerpt: At $14 million per megawatt, that works out to around $156.8 billion in annual revenue in GPU rental revenue required to actually make these data centers worth it.

from_speaker: 15.2GW of data center capacity under construction (due by the end of 2028)
around $156.8 billion in annual revenue in GPU rental revenue required to actually make these data centers worth it
our_interpretation: The claim is a calculation built on assumptions he states openly (15.2GW, PUE 1.35, $14M per MW). The arithmetic can be checked. 'Required to make these data centers worth it' is a modelling judgment with no stated basis.

Earlier in the post, the $14M per MW figure is a construction cost per MW of data-center capacity. Here it is used as an annual revenue requirement per MW. Nothing in the post explains that step, so the 'required' figure cannot be tested as a fact.
If the claim were testable, it would describe the build-out as of the post date, April 2026.
criteria.support_condition: A test would need reliable sources confirming the 15.2GW figure and an accepted basis showing that $14M per MW of critical IT per year is the revenue needed to justify these builds, plus correct arithmetic.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Arithmetic that does not produce about $156.8B from his inputs, or authoritative evidence that the inputs he presents as fact are wrong.
